ai.description: *Lycodon anamallensis* reaches 60 cm. It is dark brown with thin, white, incomplete cross-bands. It features a distinct white nuchal collar and a flattened head with a rounded snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Colombo Wolf Snake is best distinguished by its distinct, narrow white crossbars that are often broken or interrupted, contrasting with the solid bands of similar species.
ai.habitat: The Colombo Wolf Snake inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 800 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Colombo Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt geckos and small skinks among rocky crevices and urban structures.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon anamallensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon anamallensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the Anaimalai and Palani Hills at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
